## 1. Simulation and fixed-eta0 fits

Does sensitivity to the initial $\eta_0$ imply that the profiled IW ELBO has
multiple local maxima? We examine one new simulated locus, using the shared
European-like growth model from the v5 simulations.

The locus is 1 Mb, with 200,000 study individuals and 5,000 reference
individuals. The populations split $T=200$ generations ago. Recombination is
$10^{-8}$ per base per generation, and mutation is $2.36\times10^{-8}$.
We use DTWF ancestry for the first 100 generations backward in time, followed
by Hudson ancestry, retaining the specified demographic history.
We keep all shared variable biallelic SNPs with study MAF at least 1%.
This gives 1,752 SNPs and relative LD distance
$\lVert R_0-R\rVert_F/\lVert R\rVert_F=0.2625$.

We sample $L_{\mathrm{true}}=3$ causal variants without a correlation cutoff,
draw independent normal effects, and rescale them so that
$\beta^\top R\beta=h^2/(1-h^2)$ with $h^2=1\%$. Then
$$
v=R\beta+\epsilon,\qquad \epsilon\sim N(0,R/N).
$$
The master seed is 20261101. This locus was not selected based on its fitting
results. One of its three sampled effects is weak.

We fit IW with $L=10$, fixing $\eta_0$ at 21 log-spaced values from 100 to
10,000. Lambda and effect prior variances remain free; lambda is bounded by
$[10^{-5},0.2]$, and prior variances start at 0.2. SER fallback is disabled.
We use independent fits and warm starts along the grid in both directions.
The coarse fits use relative tolerance $10^{-8}$ and at most 1,000 iterations.
We then refine the range 200--600 with 25 log-spaced points, tolerance
$10^{-10}$, and at most 2,000 iterations, plus an independent fit at the best
refined grid point.

The fits used susieRobust 0.0.0.9002 and susieR 0.14.2. A local copy of the
internal fitter supplied continuation and a cached reference spectrum;
a regression check confirmed that cached cold fits match the native fitter.
This page reads the saved numerical results and regenerates the figure; it
does not rerun the simulations or fits.

```{r}
coarse <- read.csv("data/iw-eta-profile/profile_results.csv")
fine <- read.csv("data/iw-eta-profile/refined_results.csv")
cols <- c("path", "eta0_fixed", "elbo", "converged")
fits <- rbind(coarse[, cols], fine[, cols])
stopifnot(nrow(coarse) == 63, nrow(fine) == 51,
          all(coarse$converged), sum(!fine$converged) == 1)

# Highest converged ELBO found at each fixed eta0.
best_found <- function(x) {
  x <- x[x$converged, ]
  x <- x[order(-x$elbo), ]
  x <- x[!duplicated(round(x$eta0_fixed, 8)), ]
  x[order(x$eta0_fixed), ]
}
profile <- best_found(fits)
fine_profile <- best_found(fine)
```

## 2. Initialization, multiple CSs, and SER fallback

Our initialization experiments suggest a tendency: small initial $\eta_0$
can lead IW to a lower-ELBO solution with one retained credible set, which
then triggers SER fallback. Starting larger tends to help IW reach a
higher-ELBO solution with multiple credible sets and avoid fallback. Below,
independent free-$\eta_0$ fits confirm this pattern on this locus. It is not
a guarantee for other datasets, nor an estimate of how often it happens.

### Fixed-eta0 branches

The two continuation paths find different ELBO values at the same fixed
$\eta_0$. The lower branch peaks near 302, while the higher branch peaks
near 346. Their peak ELBO values differ by about 4.51.
The ascending path eventually leaves the lower branch and joins the higher
one. This is evidence of sensitivity to the optimization path, consistent
with distinct local solutions of the joint variational optimization.

```{r}
local_peaks <- function(x) {
  x <- x[order(x$eta0_fixed), ]
  y <- x$elbo
  i <- which(y[2:(length(y)-1)] > y[1:(length(y)-2)] &
             y[2:(length(y)-1)] > y[3:length(y)]) + 1L
  x[i, ]
}
lower <- local_peaks(subset(fine, path == "ascending" & converged))[1, ]
higher <- fine_profile[which.max(fine_profile$elbo), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  branch=c("Lower branch", "Higher branch"),
  eta0=c(lower$eta0_fixed, higher$eta0_fixed),
  ELBO=c(lower$elbo, higher$elbo)
), digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
```

```{r eta-profile, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.8}
oldpar <- par(mfrow=c(1, 2), mar=c(4.2, 4.5, 2.5, 1))
colors <- c(ascending="#D55E00", descending="#0072B2")
draw_profile <- function(points, envelope, xlim, ylim, title) {
  plot(envelope$eta0_fixed, envelope$elbo, type="n", log="x",
       xlim=xlim, ylim=ylim, xlab=expression("Fixed " * eta[0]),
       ylab="IW ELBO", main=title, las=1)
  for (path in names(colors)) {
    d <- points[points$path == path, ]
    d <- d[order(d$eta0_fixed), ]
    lines(d$eta0_fixed, d$elbo, col=colors[path], lwd=2)
  }
  lines(envelope$eta0_fixed, envelope$elbo, lty=2, lwd=2)
  cold <- subset(coarse, path == "cold")
  points(cold$eta0_fixed, cold$elbo, pch=21, bg="white", col="grey40")
  failed <- fits[!fits$converged, ]
  points(failed$eta0_fixed, failed$elbo, pch=4, col="red", lwd=2)
}
draw_profile(coarse, profile, c(100, 10000), range(fits$elbo),
             "Requested range")
legend("bottomleft",
       c("Low to high", "High to low", "Best converged", "Independent", "Not converged"),
       col=c(colors, "black", "grey40", "red"),
       lty=c(1, 1, 2, NA, NA), pch=c(NA, NA, NA, 1, 4),
       lwd=c(2, 2, 2, NA, 2), bty="n", cex=0.8)
draw_profile(fine, fine_profile, c(200, 600), c(9870, 9886),
             "Near the peak")
par(oldpar)
```

All 63 coarse-grid fits converged. One of the 51 refinement fits reached the
iteration cap: the ascending fit at $\eta_0=455.90$. It is marked red and
excluded from the best-converged envelope. Its neighbors show the eventual
switch to the higher branch.

To connect these branches to fine-mapping, we recovered 95% credible sets
from the saved posteriors, using exact minimum absolute correlation at least
0.5 in $R_0$ and the usual deduplication. The lower branch has one retained
CS; the higher branch has two.

```{r}
branch_cs <- read.csv("data/iw-eta-profile/branch_cs_summary.csv")
branch_cs <- subset(branch_cs, checkpoint %in% c("ascending_10", "descending_13"))
stopifnot(all(branch_cs$converged),
          identical(branch_cs$n_cs, c(1L, 2L)),
          all(branch_cs$would_trigger_fallback == (branch_cs$n_cs <= 1)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Solution=branch_cs$solution,
  eta0=branch_cs$eta0,
  ELBO=branch_cs$elbo,
  CSs=branch_cs$n_cs,
  `CS sizes`=branch_cs$cs_sizes,
  `Would trigger SER fallback`=ifelse(branch_cs$would_trigger_fallback, "Yes", "No"),
  check.names=FALSE
), digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
```

Strictly speaking, IW does not converge *to* the SER fallback. It optimizes
the IW model first. If zero or one credible set survives filtering, the
postprocessing rule substitutes an SER fit. Fallback was disabled in this
diagnostic, so the table records whether each saved IW posterior would
trigger it if enabled. The displayed ELBOs belong to the original IW fits,
not to substituted SER fits.

### Independent initializations with eta0 free

We now start four fresh fits at $\eta_0\in\{10,100,1000,10000\}$ on the
same $R_0$ and $v$. Both $\eta_0$ and $\lambda$ are learned. All other
initialization and model settings are identical, with $L=10$, relative
tolerance $10^{-8}$ and at most 3,000 iterations. Restarts are disabled;
none of these fits uses a warm start from the fixed grid. We use the native
`susie_iw()` function and enable its usual SER fallback, with partitioning
disabled. The ELBO and trajectories below are from the original IW fit,
before any fallback.

```{r}
starts <- read.csv("data/iw-eta-profile/initialization_summary.csv")
trajectories <- read.csv("data/iw-eta-profile/initialization_trajectories.csv")
stopifnot(nrow(starts) == 4, all(starts$converged),
          all(starts$core_converged), all(starts$optimizer_converged),
          all(starts$relative_change < 1e-8),
          all(starts$fallback == (starts$raw_n_cs <= 1)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Initial eta0`=starts$initial_eta0,
  `Learned eta0`=starts$eta0,
  `IW ELBO`=starts$core_elbo,
  Iterations=starts$iterations,
  `IW CSs`=starts$raw_n_cs,
  `SER fallback`=ifelse(starts$fallback, "Yes", "No"),
  Converged=starts$converged, check.names=FALSE
), digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
```

All four fits converge. Starts at 10, 100 and 1,000 reach the lower branch
near learned $\eta_0=300$, retain one CS and trigger SER fallback. The
10,000 start reaches the higher branch near learned $\eta_0=351$, retains
two CSs and does not trigger fallback. Its core ELBO is about 4.51 higher.
The retained CS sizes are 2 for the lower solutions and 1 and 2 for the
higher solution.

```{r initialization-trajectories, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.8}
oldpar <- par(mfrow=c(1, 2), mar=c(4.2, 4.5, 2.5, 1))
start_colors <- c("#777777", "#E69F00", "#D55E00", "#0072B2")
xlim <- range(trajectories$iteration)
plot(NA, xlim=xlim, ylim=range(trajectories$eta0),
     xlab="Iteration", ylab=expression("Learned " * eta[0]),
     main="Eta0 after each update", las=1)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(starts))) {
  d <- subset(trajectories, initial_eta0 == starts$initial_eta0[i])
  lines(d$iteration, d$eta0, col=start_colors[i], lwd=2, lty=i)
  points(tail(d$iteration, 1), tail(d$eta0, 1), col=start_colors[i], pch=19)
}
legend("bottomright", paste("Initial eta0 =", starts$initial_eta0),
       col=start_colors, lty=seq_len(nrow(starts)), lwd=2, bty="n", cex=0.8)
plot(NA, xlim=xlim, ylim=c(9878, 9886),
     xlab="Iteration", ylab="Core IW ELBO",
     main="ELBO near the endpoints", las=1)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(starts))) {
  d <- subset(trajectories, initial_eta0 == starts$initial_eta0[i])
  lines(d$iteration, d$elbo, col=start_colors[i], lwd=2, lty=i)
  points(tail(d$iteration, 1), tail(d$elbo, 1), col=start_colors[i], pch=19)
}
par(oldpar)
```

The left panel starts after the first update, so its first plotted eta0
values differ from the supplied initial values. The right panel zooms in
on the final ELBO range; earlier lower values are outside the plotting
window. Points mark each fit's stopping iteration.

This gives two distinct groups of numerically converged endpoints on the
same dataset. The three lower endpoints differ slightly because convergence
uses a finite ELBO-change tolerance. These are not proofs of exact stationary
points or global optima. In particular, the learned concentrations are fairly
close even though the initial values differ greatly: initialization affects
which posterior solution is reached, not just the final concentration.

The earlier optional 10,000-start run at tolerance $10^{-10}$ was stopped;
the new comparison above is complete and uses the same $10^{-8}$ tolerance
for all four starts. All traces and endpoint diagnostics are saved. The
fitting script is `code/iw-eta-profile/initializations.R`; it runs from the
original local experiment directory, where the LD matrices and pinned R
libraries are retained.

## 3. One peak in the best-found profile

The ideal profiled ELBO is
$$
F(\eta_0)=\max_{q,\lambda,V}\mathcal{L}(q,\lambda,V;\eta_0),
$$
where $q$ is the variational distribution and $V$ denotes the effect prior
variances. Profiling takes the best solution over these other quantities at
each $\eta_0$. A lower optimization branch can therefore disappear from the
profile wherever another branch has higher ELBO.

The black envelope approximates this maximization using the converged fits
we found. On the refined grid it has one local maximum, near $\eta_0=346$:

```{r}
peaks <- local_peaks(fine_profile)
stopifnot(nrow(peaks) == 1)
knitr::kable(peaks[, c("eta0_fixed", "elbo")], digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
```

Thus initialization sensitivity does not by itself imply two local maxima
of the profiled ELBO. This example supports the concern about different
optimization branches, but does not establish two profile maxima. The
envelope is the best found, not a certified global optimum; a finite grid
cannot exclude narrower or undiscovered peaks. One locus also does not tell
us how frequently this occurs.

The saved settings and simulation seeds are in
`data/iw-eta-profile/settings.json` and `data/iw-eta-profile/metadata.json`.
